[[File:AshokDas.jpg|thumb|Ashok Das]]
'''Ashok Das''' is an Indian-American physicist. He is professor of physics at [[University of Rochester]] and adjunct professor of physics at both Saha Institute of Nuclear Physics, Kolkata, India and Institute of Physics, Bhubaneswar, India.

==Early life and education==
Das was born in [[Puri, Odisha]], on March 23, 1953. He received his [[Bachelor of Science|BS]] (with honors) in 1972 and [[Master of Science|MS]] in [[physics]] in 1974 from the [[University of Delhi]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ashok Das |url=https://www.sas.rochester.edu/pas/people/faculty/das_ashok/index.html |access-date=2023-02-20 |website=www.sas.rochester.edu |language=en-US}}</ref> He did his graduate studies in supersymmetry and supergravity at State University of New York at Stony Brook. He received his PhD in 1977.

==Career==
Das was a research associate at the [[City College of New York]], the [[University of Maryland, College Park|University of Maryland]], and [[Rutgers University]]. He was promoted to professor in 1993 and has been employed at the [[University of Rochester]] since 1982.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.rochester.edu/news/experts/index.php?id=65 |title=Faculty Experts: Ashok Das |access-date=2014-08-27 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140904030338/http://www.rochester.edu/news/experts/index.php?id=65 |archive-date=2014-09-04 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Das' research is in the area of theoretical [[High-energy physics]]. His research has focused on questions of symmetry in the fundamental laws of nature. He has worked on nonlinear integrable systems, finite temperature field theories, generalization of the [[Standard Model]] to incorporate [[CP violation]], and problems in [[Quantum field theory]] and [[String theory]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ashok Das |url=https://www.sas.rochester.edu/pas/people/faculty/das_ashok/index.html |access-date=2024-02-02 |website=www.sas.rochester.edu |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.pas.rochester.edu/people/faculty/das_ashok/index.html | title=Ashok das }}</ref>

In 2002, Das became a [[fellow]] of the [[American Physical Society]] "for contributions in the areas of [[supergravity]], [[Integrable system|integrable models]], and [[Finite Temperature Field Theory|finite temperature field theory]]."<ref>[http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=D&year=2013&unit_id=&institution= APS Fellows Archive]</ref> In 2006, he was awarded a [[Fulbright Program|Fulbright]] scholarship to teach physics in Brazil.<ref>University of Rochester. ''Physics professor Ashok Das Receives Fulbright to Teach in Brazil [http://www.rochester.edu/news/show.php?id=2693]''</ref>

Ashok Das has written books and monographs on various disciplines of theoretical physics at the advanced undergraduate and graduate level. Some of his books include: ''[https://www.worldscientific.com/worldscibooks/10.1142/11339#t=aboutBook A Path Integral Approach]'' ([[World Scientific]] publishers), ''Finite Temperature Field Theory'' ([[World Scientific]] publishers), ''Integrable Models'' (World Scientific Lecture Notes in Physics), ''Lectures on Gravitation'' (World Scientific publishers), and ''Lectures on [[Electromagnetism]]''.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Das| first=Ashok| url=https://www.worldscientific.com/worldscibooks/10.1142/8805#t=aboutBook |title=Lectures on Electromagnetism | edition=2 | publisher=World Scientific |isbn=978-981-4508-26-1 |date=August 2013| doi=10.1142/8805}}</ref>
